bugfix.what: Fixing broken product behavior: a bug, a crash, a regression, an incident, wrong output.
bugfix.not_for: Fixing CI, build, release or tooling problems (infra). Writing about a bug without changing code (docs).
examples: the login page 404s after sign in, fix it
the hook crashes on empty input

feature.what: Adding a new capability: a new command, endpoint, skill, option, integration or screen.
feature.not_for: Changing CI or tooling (infra). Restructuring existing code without new behavior (refactor).
examples: add an opt-in provider for the session category
build a new export endpoint

docs.what: Writing or updating documentation, research, analysis, plans, reports, digests, status summaries, or answering a question without shipping code.
docs.not_for: User interface or visual work (design). Code changes (bugfix, feature, refactor).
examples: research this vendor and write an adoption plan
write the daily digest
explain how the auth flow works

refactor.what: Restructuring or cleaning up existing code with no behavior change: renames, splitting files, removing dead code.
examples: split this 900 line module into three files
remove the dead compatibility shims

infra.what: CI pipelines, builds, releases, deploys, dependency bumps, dev tooling, git and merge operations, and coordinating or dispatching other agent sessions.
infra.not_for: Product bugs surfaced by CI (bugfix). Writing tests (testing).
examples: fix the failing release workflow
bump the node version across repos
run the merge train and dispatch lanes

perf.what: Making something faster or cheaper: latency, memory, bundle size, token or compute cost.
examples: cut hook startup time
reduce the bundle size

design.what: User interface, UX and visual styling: layouts, pages, components, colors, how something looks to a person.
design.not_for: Software architecture or system design documents (docs). Restructuring code (refactor).
examples: restyle the settings page
fix the RTL layout of the dashboard

testing.what: Writing, running or fixing tests, QA passes, verifying that a change works.
testing.not_for: Reviewing someone else's pull request (review). Fixing the product code a test exposed (bugfix).
examples: add unit tests for the parser
QA the checkout flow

review.what: Reviewing a pull request or another agent's change and giving a verdict such as land or hold.
review.not_for: Writing tests yourself (testing). Fixing the code under review (bugfix).
examples: review PR 123 and give a verdict
reviewer lane for the open orchestkit PRs
